detections.sql:
SELECT
  u.user_id,
  u.username,
  le.event_id AS login_event_id,
  le.created_at AS login_time,
  le.country AS login_country,
  le.device_type AS login_device_type,
  t.txn_id AS transaction_id,
  t.created_at AS transaction_time,
  t.amount_usd,
  t.txn_type,
  u.risk_level
FROM users AS u
JOIN login_events AS le
  ON u.user_id = le.user_id
JOIN transactions AS t
  ON u.user_id = t.user_id
WHERE
  UPPER(le.status) LIKE '%SUCCESS%' AND UPPER(u.risk_level) IN ('%MEDIUM%', '%LOW%') AND t.created_at BETWEEN le.created_at AND DATETIME(le.created_at, '+24 hours') AND UPPER(t.txn_type) IN ('%WITHDRAWAL%', '%INTERNATIONAL_TRANSFER%') AND t.amount_usd > (
    SELECT
      AVG(t_past.amount_usd) + 3 * SQRT(AVG(t_past.amount_usd * t_past.amount_usd) - (AVG(t_past.amount_usd) * AVG(t_past.amount_usd)))
    FROM transactions AS t_past
    WHERE
      t_past.user_id = t.user_id AND t_past.created_at < t.created_at AND t_past.created_at >= DATETIME(t.created_at, '-90 days') AND t_past.amount_usd IS NOT NULL
  ) AND (
    NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM login_events AS le_past_country
      WHERE
        le_past_country.user_id = le.user_id AND le_past_country.created_at < le.created_at AND le_past_country.created_at >= DATETIME(le.created_at, '-90 days') AND UPPER(le_past_country.status) LIKE '%SUCCESS%' AND UPPER(le_past_country.country) LIKE UPPER(le.country)
    ) OR NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM login_events AS le_past_device
      WHERE
        le_past_device.user_id = le.user_id AND le_past_device.created_at < le.created_at AND le_past_device.created_at >= DATETIME(le.created_at, '-90 days') AND UPPER(le_past_device.status) LIKE '%SUCCESS%' AND UPPER(le_past_device.device_type) LIKE UPPER(le.device_type)
    )
  );

SELECT DISTINCT u.username
FROM users u
JOIN transactions t ON u.user_id = t.user_id
WHERE
    (UPPER(u.kyc_status) LIKE '%PENDING%' OR UPPER(u.kyc_status) LIKE '%FAILED%')
    AND
    (UPPER(u.risk_level) LIKE '%HIGH%' OR UPPER(u.risk_level) LIKE '%CRITICAL%' OR u.risk_score > 8.0)
    AND
    t.created_at >= strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S', date('2026-04-22', '-7 days'))
GROUP BY u.user_id, u.username
HAVING COUNT(t.txn_id) > 3;

detections.mission_name: PEP High-Value Transactions with New Methods
detections.sql:
WITH PEP_New_Method_Txns AS (
    SELECT
        t.user_id,
        u.username,
        t.amount_usd,
        DATE(t.created_at) AS transaction_day,
        t.payment_method,
        t.instrument,
        t.created_at
    FROM
        users u
    JOIN
        transactions t ON u.user_id = t.user_id
    WHERE
        u.is_pep = 1
        AND (UPPER(t.txn_type) LIKE '%WITHDRAWAL%' OR UPPER(t.txn_type) LIKE '%INTERNATIONAL_TRANSFER%')
        AND (UPPER(t.flag_reason) LIKE '%NONE%' OR UPPER(t.flag_reason) LIKE '%AUTOMATICALLY_CLEARED%')
        AND t.created_at >= DATE('2026-04-22', '-60 days')
        AND NOT EXISTS (
            SELECT 1
            FROM transactions t_prev
            WHERE
                t_prev.user_id = t.user_id
                AND t_prev.created_at BETWEEN DATE(t.created_at, '-90 days') AND DATE(t.created_at, '-1 day')
                AND (
                    UPPER(t_prev.payment_method) = UPPER(t.payment_method)
                    OR UPPER(t_prev.instrument) = UPPER(t.instrument)
                )
        )
),
Daily_PEP_Txn_Totals AS (
    SELECT
        user_id,
        username,
        transaction_day,
        SUM(amount_usd) AS daily_total_amount_usd
    FROM
        PEP_New_Method_Txns
    GROUP BY
        user_id,
        username,
        transaction_day
)
SELECT
    user_id,
    username,
    AVG(daily_total_amount_usd) AS average_daily_amount_usd
FROM
    Daily_PEP_Txn_Totals
GROUP BY
    user_id,
    username
HAVING
    AVG(daily_total_amount_usd) > 10000;

This monitors for PEPs attempting to bypass existing controls.

detections.sql:
WITH LoginFailureSuccessCounts AS (
    SELECT
        country,
        device_type,
        SUM(CASE WHEN UPPER(status) LIKE '%FAILED%' AND (UPPER(failure_reason) LIKE '%AUTHENTICATION_ERROR%' OR UPPER(failure_reason) LIKE '%TEMPORARY_LOCKOUT%') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_login_count,
        SUM(CASE WHEN UPPER(status) LIKE '%SUCCESS%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS success_login_count
    FROM login_events
    GROUP BY country, device_type
),
LoginRatios AS (
    SELECT
        country,
        device_type,
        CAST(failed_login_count AS REAL) / NULLIF(success_login_count, 0) AS failure_success_ratio
    FROM LoginFailureSuccessCounts
),
GlobalAverageRatio AS (
    SELECT AVG(failure_success_ratio) AS global_avg_ratio
    FROM LoginRatios
    WHERE failure_success_ratio IS NOT NULL
),
HighRatioCombinations AS (
    SELECT lr.country, lr.device_type
    FROM LoginRatios lr, GlobalAverageRatio gar
    WHERE lr.failure_success_ratio IS NOT NULL AND lr.failure_success_ratio >= (3 * gar.global_avg_ratio)
),
RelevantFailedLoginEvents AS (
    SELECT
        le.event_id,
        le.user_id,
        le.created_at AS failed_login_time,
        le.country,
        le.device_type
    FROM login_events le
    JOIN HighRatioCombinations hrc ON le.country = hrc.country AND le.device_type = hrc.device_type
    WHERE UPPER(le.status) LIKE '%FAILED%'
      AND (UPPER(le.failure_reason) LIKE '%AUTHENTICATION_ERROR%' OR UPPER(le.failure_reason) LIKE '%TEMPORARY_LOCKOUT%')
),
UserTransactionData AS (
    SELECT
        rfle.user_id,
        rfle.failed_login_time,
        rfle.country,
        rfle.device_type,
        -- Calculate 7-day sum of transactions before the failed login event
        COALESCE((
            SELECT SUM(t_pre.amount_usd)
            FROM transactions t_pre
            WHERE t_pre.user_id = rfle.user_id
              AND t_pre.created_at BETWEEN DATETIME(rfle.failed_login_time, '-7 days') AND rfle.failed_login_time
        ), 0.0) AS sum_amount_7d_pre,
        -- Calculate 24-hour sum of transactions after the failed login event
        COALESCE((
            SELECT SUM(t_post.amount_usd)
            FROM transactions t_post
            WHERE t_post.user_id = rfle.user_id
              AND t_post.created_at BETWEEN rfle.failed_login_time AND DATETIME(rfle.failed_login_time, '+1 day')
        ), 0.0) AS sum_amount_24h_post
    FROM RelevantFailedLoginEvents rfle
)
SELECT DISTINCT
    utd.country,
    utd.device_type
FROM UserTransactionData utd
WHERE
    (utd.sum_amount_7d_pre / 7.0) > 0.0 -- Ensure there was a non-zero average to decrease from
    AND utd.sum_amount_24h_post < (utd.sum_amount_7d_pre / 7.0) * 0.5;

detections.mission_name: Dormant Account Activation and High-Risk Exploit
detections.sql:
WITH UserActivityTimelines AS (
    -- Combine all relevant timestamps (successful logins, all transactions) for dormancy detection.
    -- This helps determine the "last activity before login" for identifying 90+ day gaps.
    SELECT user_id, created_at FROM login_events WHERE UPPER(status) LIKE '%SUCCESS%'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT user_id, created_at FROM transactions
),
PotentialActivations AS (
    -- Identify successful logins that occur after a 90+ day period of no activity.
    -- This is the 'first successful login after this dormant period'.
    SELECT
        le.user_id,
        le.created_at AS activation_login_time,
        MAX(CASE WHEN uat.created_at < le.created_at THEN uat.created_at ELSE NULL END) AS last_activity_before_login
    FROM login_events le
    LEFT JOIN UserActivityTimelines uat ON le.user_id = uat.user_id
    WHERE UPPER(le.status) LIKE '%SUCCESS%'
    GROUP BY le.user_id, le.event_id, le.created_at
    HAVING (last_activity_before_login IS NULL -- Handles the case where it's the very first activity for the user
            OR JULIANDAY(le.created_at) - JULIANDAY(last_activity_before_login) > 90)
),
DormancyContext AS (
    -- For each potential activation, define its dormancy context,
    -- specifically the 90-day window for calculating the previous average amount.
    SELECT
        pa.user_id,
        pa.activation_login_time,
        pa.last_activity_before_login,
        -- The 90-day average window ends on the 'last_activity_before_login' date.
        -- It starts 89 days prior to that. If no prior activity, use a very old date.
        CASE
            WHEN pa.last_activity_before_login IS NOT NULL THEN DATE(pa.last_activity_before_login, '-89 days')
            ELSE '1900-01-01' -- Far past date to ensure 0 average if no prior transactions
        END AS avg_window_start,
        pa.last_activity_before_login AS avg_window_end
    FROM PotentialActivations pa
),
SuspiciousTransactions AS (
    -- Find 'WITHDRAWAL' or 'TRANSFER' transactions that occur within 7 days
    -- of the 'activation_login_time'.
    SELECT
        dc.user_id,
        u.full_name, -- Using full_name as per actual schema, aliased to 'username' in final select
        dc.activation_login_time,
        dc.last_activity_before_login,
        dc.avg_window_start,
        dc.avg_window_end,
        t.txn_id,
        t.created_at AS txn_time,
        t.amount_usd,
        t.txn_type,
        t.instrument,
        t.payment_method
    FROM DormancyContext dc
    JOIN transactions t ON dc.user_id = t.user_id
    JOIN users u ON dc.user_id = u.user_id -- To get user's full_name
    WHERE JULIANDAY(t.created_at) >= JULIANDAY(dc.activation_login_time)
      AND JULIANDAY(t.created_at) < JULIANDAY(dc.activation_login_time) + 7
      AND (UPPER(t.txn_type) LIKE '%WITHDRAWAL%' OR UPPER(t.txn_type) LIKE '%TRANSFER%')
),
TransactionsWithPreviousAvg AS (
    -- Calculate the average amount_usd for the user in the 90 days prior to the dormancy start.
    SELECT
        st.*,
        COALESCE(
            (SELECT AVG(t_prev.amount_usd)
             FROM transactions t_prev
             WHERE t_prev.user_id = st.user_id
               AND t_prev.created_at >= st.avg_window_start
               AND t_prev.created_at <= st.avg_window_end
            ), 0
        ) AS previous_90_day_avg_amount_usd
    FROM SuspiciousTransactions st
)
SELECT
    twpa.full_name AS username,
    twpa.txn_id,
    twpa.txn_time,
    twpa.amount_usd,
    twpa.txn_type,
    twpa.instrument,
    twpa.payment_method,
    twpa.activation_login_time,
    twpa.last_activity_before_login,
    twpa.previous_90_day_avg_amount_usd
FROM TransactionsWithPreviousAvg twpa
WHERE twpa.amount_usd > (twpa.previous_90_day_avg_amount_usd * 5)
  AND (
        -- Check if the 'instrument' of the suspicious transaction was NOT seen in the last 180 days.
        -- Handles both NULL and non-NULL instruments based on strict LIKE rule.
        (
            (twpa.instrument IS NULL AND NOT EXISTS ( -- If current instrument is NULL, check if NULL instrument was seen before
                SELECT 1 FROM transactions t_hist WHERE t_hist.user_id = twpa.user_id
                AND JULIANDAY(t_hist.created_at) >= JULIANDAY(twpa.txn_time) - 180
                AND JULIANDAY(t_hist.created_at) < JULIANDAY(twpa.txn_time)
                AND t_hist.instrument IS NULL
            ))
            OR
            (twpa.instrument IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS ( -- If current instrument is not NULL, check for similar instrument (partial match)
                SELECT 1 FROM transactions t_hist WHERE t_hist.user_id = twpa.user_id
                AND JULIANDAY(t_hist.created_at) >= JULIANDAY(twpa.txn_time) - 180
                AND JULIANDAY(t_hist.created_at) < JULIANDAY(twpa.txn_time)
                AND UPPER(t_hist.instrument) LIKE '%' || UPPER(twpa.instrument) || '%'
            ))
        )
        OR
        -- Check if the 'payment_method' of the suspicious transaction was NOT seen in the last 180 days.
        -- Handles both NULL and non-NULL payment_methods based on strict LIKE rule.
        (
            (twpa.payment_method IS NULL AND NOT EXISTS ( -- If current payment_method is NULL, check if NULL payment_method was seen before
                SELECT 1 FROM transactions t_hist WHERE t_hist.user_id = twpa.user_id
                AND JULIANDAY(t_hist.created_at) >= JULIANDAY(twpa.txn_time) - 180
                AND JULIANDAY(t_hist.created_at) < JULIANDAY(twpa.txn_time)
                AND t_hist.payment_method IS NULL
            ))
            OR
            (twpa.payment_method IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS ( -- If current payment_method is not NULL, check for similar payment_method (partial match)
                SELECT 1 FROM transactions t_hist WHERE t_hist.user_id = twpa.user_id
                AND JULIANDAY(t_hist.created_at) >= JULIANDAY(twpa.txn_time) - 180
                AND JULIANDAY(t_hist.created_at) < JULIANDAY(twpa.txn_time)
                AND UPPER(t_hist.payment_method) LIKE '%' || UPPER(twpa.payment_method) || '%'
            ))
        )
      );

visualization_config.description: The query identifies highly specific fraud patterns (account takeover/sleeper activation) involving multiple variables like dormancy periods, login times, and novel payment methods. A table is the most appropriate format for a fraud investigation as it allows analysts to review all granular details and contextual timestamps side-by-side.

detections.insight: This query result highlights a critical and immediate financial risk across 56 user accounts. The consistent pattern of accounts dormant for over 90 days initiating significant 'WITHDRAWAL' transactions within seven days of a new login, coupled with the use of previously unrecorded payment methods and an average previous 90-day transaction amount of zero, strongly indicates a high probability of account takeover (ATO) or malicious sleeper account activation. These activities pose a direct threat of financial loss to the enterprise or its customers, as funds are being exfiltrated via suspicious means, and could lead to significant reputational damage and potential regulatory scrutiny.
detections.recommendation:
1. **Immediate Transaction & Account Freezing:** Implement an emergency protocol to immediately flag and, where possible, temporarily halt processing for all 56 identified withdrawal transactions. Concurrently, initiate out-of-band contact with the legitimate account holders to verify transaction legitimacy and account control, while conducting a full security review of these compromised accounts. 
2. **Proactive Risk Rule Enhancement:** Develop and deploy a real-time automated risk rule that triggers an immediate security challenge (e.g., mandatory multi-factor authentication, enhanced identity verification) or temporary transaction hold for any high-value withdrawal or transfer activity from accounts dormant for more than 90 days that attempts to use a payment method or instrument not observed in the user's last 180 days of activity. Review and strengthen dormant account reactivation policies, potentially including a mandatory waiting period for new payment method usage.

This could indicate an account takeover or a sleeper account activation.

narrative.executive_summary: Your platform currently faces a critical and immediate financial risk stemming from a sophisticated exploit targeting dormant accounts. We have identified 56 user accounts, previously inactive for over 90 days, that have recently initiated significant withdrawal transactions using previously unrecorded payment methods shortly after reactivation. This consistent pattern strongly suggests a coordinated fraudulent activity, posing a direct threat to customer assets and platform integrity. Immediate intervention is required to contain this exploit and mitigate potential losses.

threat_vectors.name: Dormant Account Activation and High-Risk Exploit
threat_vectors.description: A critical financial exploit impacting 56 user accounts, where dormant accounts (inactive >90 days) are reactivated, followed by significant withdrawals using new, unrecorded payment methods within seven days. This indicates potential account takeover and fraud.

immediate_actions: Immediately freeze or place under enhanced review the 56 identified accounts to prevent further unauthorized transactions and potential financial losses.
Launch a forensic investigation into the reactivation methods and associated new payment methods to identify compromise vectors and the extent of the breach.
Implement an emergency policy requiring mandatory multi-factor authentication and a 48-hour hold for new payment method usage on all reactivated dormant accounts.
Quantify the potential financial exposure and prepare a communication plan for affected customers.
monitoring_recommendations: Prioritize and enhance real-time monitoring for dormant account reactivation, specifically flagging logins followed by rapid transaction attempts or new payment method additions.
Conduct an expedited audit of all dormant account security protocols and reactivation workflows to identify and mitigate systemic vulnerabilities.
Verify the operational status and data collection for all other critical intelligence missions, addressing any 'no data found' issues to ensure comprehensive threat visibility.
